Command: python3 docs/dev/measurements/probe_b109_reseed_twin.py --trials 21
  (21 trials/cell; trial 0 is DROPPED from every median/spread below --
  see "MEASUREMENT CAVEAT" -- so the summary reads as 20 trials/cell)
Trials: 21 per (pattern, subject, cc, variant) cell, 60 cells x 2 variants
  = 120 driver invocations, plus one compile-only candidate-density probe
  per pattern x subject (30 cells, no timing)

WHY THIS PROBE EXISTS: pcrec inbox I-114 hand-wrote a twin of
[OPT-HYB-RESEED] (the VM hybrid's unanchored retry loop re-seeding
`attempt_position` from the DFA prefilter after every failed attempt,
not only under an MRL clamp) on three lookaround patterns at pin
a32bc86e, measured it on an Apple M1 (Mac, gcc-16, box not quiet --
SCRATCH TIER, mechanism/direction only) and asked this project to
confirm on x86: answers identical, timing reproduced or not, and in
particular whether x86 shows the SAME dense-candidate slowdown the Mac
run found on `asr-lb-fixed` (`(?<=é)x`) -- ×0.81-0.90, twin SLOWER --
on its two densest-candidate subjects.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT (found during this run, not predicted by I-114): this
box's `scaling_governor` is `schedutil`, and several cells' trial 0 (and
occasionally trials 1-7) ran at what reads as a throttled/ramping
frequency state -- e.g. `row11_fixed/synth-64k-asc/gcc/orig`'s raw trials
were 2355,2348,2340,2352,2332,1971,1100,929,173,173,... (an order of
magnitude down before settling). A same-invocation repeat with 21 trials
of one cell (not archived; done ad hoc while building this probe) found
an 11-trial run's UNFILTERED median 2.4x an equivalent 21-trial run's
median for the identical binaries and subject purely from where in the
ramp the median trial landed. The summary below drops trial 0 (never a
full fix -- see the one cell below whose trials 1-7 still ramp) and
reports median + full max-min spread over the rest so a ramp-contaminated
cell is visible in its own spread column rather than hidden. Absolute
timings should be read as APPROXIMATE; the orig-vs-twin RATIO within one
cell (compiled, subject-loaded, and measured within the same script
invocation, seconds apart) is the reliable comparison this file supports
-- not a cross-run or cross-machine comparison of absolute µs.
